To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bunch distribution is not affected outside the transition energy, and that the bunch distribution in the transition region is affected by the high-frequency RF voltage, but the effect can be minimized by reducing the high-frequency RF amplitude and the high-frequency RF field error.

the induced 160 MHz RF voltage on the RHIC 26.7-MHz bunch distribution is not important outside the RHIC transition energy region due primarily to the synchrotron oscillation mixing, while it is significant at the transition energy due to the lack of the synchroton oscillation mixing.

the induced high-frequency voltage during the bunch motion at transition energy region is a critical issue for the bunch distribution and that the bunch distribution is sensitive to the high-frequency RF system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the induced voltage at the transition energy on the bunch distribution.

the effect of the induced high frequency RF voltage on the phase space growth during the bunch acceleration in the transition energy region, and we find that the induced high-frequency voltage is the most significant source in the phase space growth.
the effect of the induced high frequency RF voltage on the beam distribution in the transition energy region of a storage ring.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bunch distribution is stable in the transition energy region if the remnant 160 MHz RF voltage V/sub 2/ is smaller than 25 kV.

the tolerable induced high-frequency voltage is V/sub2/<25 k V at the transition energy for a bunch length of 2 pi radians, and that this induced voltage is not significant for the bunch length outside the transition energy.

the bunch distribution is stable at the transition energy if the following two criteria are fulfilled: (1) V/sub 1/>/spl sim/25 kV, and (2) the phase error of the 160-MHz stable phase is less than 0.5 radian.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a computer program to analyze the effect of the induced voltage in a high-frequency RF system on the bunch motion.
we have shown that the induced high-frequency voltage is tolerable at the transition energy and the error in the stable RF phase plays little role.
, in the RHIC, the bunch lengthening due to the induced high-frequency voltage is not serious.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the induced voltage on a bunch during acceleration through the transition is tolerable.
the bunch distribution in the high-frequency phase is almost unaffected by the induced voltage.
we have shown that the induced voltage is not important for the bunch stability in the high-frequency storage RF system.
